units.title: Pesukei Dezimra – Baruch She’amar
units.english: Blessed is He who spoke, and the world came into being.
units.commentary: In the Conservative tradition this opening of the morning praises focuses on God as Creator through speech. Kavannah is directed toward recognizing the ongoing creative power of the Divine Word.
units.kavannahPrompt: Before continuing, take a moment to feel gratitude that the world exists because God spoke.

units.title: From Mesillat Yesharim – on Kavannah
units.english: The beginning of all avodah is the intention of the heart. Without kavannah, the external act remains incomplete.
units.commentary: Classic Musar teaching appropriate for intermediate Conservative study: practical focus on directing the heart during prayer and daily life.
units.kavannahPrompt: Where in your davening today can you strengthen your kavannah?

units.title: Symbolic Light – a Conservative framing
units.english: The light of the first day is understood in many traditional sources as a spiritual light hidden for the righteous. For intermediate study we focus on its ethical and symbolic meaning: clarity and kindness in our actions.
units.commentary: Presented within Conservative bounds – symbolic and ethical emphasis, not deep theosophy.
units.kavannahPrompt: How can the idea of hidden light inspire one act of kindness today?

units.title: Psalm 145 (Ashrei) – selected verse
units.transliteration: Tov Adonai lakol verachamav al kol ma’asav
units.english: The Lord is good to all, and His mercy is upon all His works.
units.commentary: Traditional Conservative reading emphasizes universal divine compassion and the call to emulate it in our own conduct.
units.kavannahPrompt: As you recite Ashrei this morning, which of God’s works around you invites your gratitude?

notes: Generated for Masorti / Conservative – Intermediate. Focus on kavannah and traditional sources.
